key_insight: VOID extends video object removal beyond appearance-level fixes by learning to restore physically plausible scene dynamics (e.g., collisions, motion changes) after an object is removed, producing coherent spatio-temporal inpainting.
problem_solved: Existing video inpainting methods can reconstruct occluded pixels and correct appearance artifacts but fail when the removed object caused interactions with the scene (collisions, displaced objects, secondary motion), yielding implausible results; VOID addresses these interaction-driven failures.
method: Generate training data with controlled object interactions (simulated or synthesized) so the model sees examples of post-removal scenes requiring dynamic corrections.
Learn a spatio-temporal inpainting model that jointly predicts appearance and interaction-consistent motion, guided by physics-aware or interaction-consistency objectives.
Combine appearance restoration with motion/trajectory correction and secondary-effect refinement (shadows, reflections) to produce globally plausible video edits.
impact: Provides a practical path toward realistic, interaction-aware video editing and synthesis—useful for film VFX, augmented reality, and robust video generative models—and demonstrates training strategies for integrating physics/interaction priors into generative pipelines.

paper_title: VOID: Video Object and Interaction Deletion
paper_authors: Saman Motamed, William Harvey, Benjamin Klein, Luc Van Gool, Zhuoning Yuan
